mainTopic: Spices and salt in hot food on שבת, and placing vessels to catch or protect things on שבת (common versus uncommon protection).
overview: The משנה lets a person put spices into a bowl or tureen on שבת, because these are secondary vessels. רבי יהודה says spices may go into anything except food that contains vinegar or fish brine. A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה is being lenient: even boiling pots are fine, as long as there is no vinegar or brine. The גמרא then discusses salt and gives two versions of a debate between רב יוסף and אביי. In one version, salt cooks even in a כלי שני, and this disagrees with רב נחמן. In the other version, salt does not cook even in a כלי ראשון, and this matches רב נחמן. A new משנה forbids placing a vessel under a lamp on שבת to catch dripping oil. רב חסדא rules that one may not place a vessel under a hen to catch its egg, but may cover the egg to protect it. רבה explains that the Sages permitted protection only in common situations, and he defends this rule against אביי's two challenges: new barrels and falling sparks are both common.

steps.title: Spices may be placed into a bowl or tureen
steps.stepSummary: The משנה permits putting spices into a קערה or תמחוי, which are secondary vessels, on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: However, one may place spices into a bowl or into a tureen.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a היתר. Spices may be put into a bowl or serving dish, because food that has been poured into these vessels does not cook the spices.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, the משנה forbade adding spices to a boiling pot taken off the fire, because that is בישול. The word "אבל" (however) marks the contrast: a קערה or תמחוי is a כלי שני, which does not have the power to cook.

keyTerms.meaning: A bowl. Hot food is poured into it from the pot, so it is a secondary vessel.
A large serving dish or tureen. It is also a secondary vessel.
Spices. They are the subject of this משנה.
A secondary vessel. It holds food poured from the cooking pot and generally does not cook.

steps.confusionAlert: The word "אבל" connects back to the previous line of the משנה, which is not here. That line says spices may NOT be put into a boiling pot (אילפס or קדירה) taken off the fire. Without that background, this line seems to come out of nowhere.

phrases.notes: Contrasts with the earlier ban on putting spices into boiling pots.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's ruling on boiling pots by giving the permitted case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spices may be placed into a כלי שני such as a bowl or tureen on שבת.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: spices go into anything except vinegar or brine
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rules that spices may be put into anything, except food that contains vinegar or fish brine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: One may place spices into anything, except something that contains vinegar or fish brine.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives his own opinion: spices are allowed everywhere, with one exception, which is food containing vinegar or fish brine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vinegar and brine are sharp liquids, and they cook the spices more strongly. What is unclear is which part of the משנה רבי יהודה is responding to. "לכל" (into anything) could mean even boiling pots, or it could mean only bowls. The גמרא will ask exactly this.

keyTerms.meaning: Vinegar. It is a sharp liquid that helps cook spices.
Brine from salted fish. It is also a sharp liquid.

phrases.notes: It is unclear what "everything" includes. This sets up the גמרא's question.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לַכֹּל הוּא נוֹתֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting opinion to the תנא קמא of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spices may be put into anything except food containing vinegar or fish brine.

steps.title: Is רבי יהודה being lenient or strict?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יהודה is commenting on the first clause, which would make him lenient, or on the last clause, which would make him strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A question was asked: Is רבי יהודה referring to the first clause, and being lenient? Or perhaps he is referring to the last clause, and being strict?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises an open question about what רבי יהודה meant. It is setting up a search for evidence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: he is responding to the first clause, so he permits spices even in a boiling pot unless vinegar or brine is inside. That is a קולא. Option two: he is responding to the last clause, so he agrees that boiling pots are forbidden, and he forbids even a bowl if it contains vinegar or brine. That is a חומרא.

keyTerms.meaning: "It was asked of them." This is a formula for a genuine open question.
The first clause of a משנה.
The last clause of a משנה.
Stands on, meaning is referring to.

steps.confusionAlert: The exception (vinegar and brine) is the same in both readings. What changes is the baseline. Under the רישא reading, boiling pots become permitted. Under the סיפא reading, bowls become partly forbidden.

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
Is Rabbi Yehuda referring to the first clause, and being lenient,
phrases.notes: In this reading, even boiling pots are permitted unless they contain vinegar or brine.

phrases.english: or perhaps he is referring to the last clause, and being strict?
phrases.notes: In this reading, even a bowl is forbidden if it contains vinegar or brine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the meaning of רבי יהודה's statement in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which clause of the משנה רבי יהודה is responding to, and therefore whether his view is lenient or strict.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי יהודה is lenient
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה permitting spices in all pots, even boiling ones, except those with vinegar or brine. This proves he is lenient about the רישא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as it was taught: רבי יהודה says: Into all stew pots one may place spices; into all pots, even boiling ones, one may place spices, except for something containing vinegar or brine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by bringing a ברייתא. In it, רבי יהודה clearly permits spices even in boiling pots.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "קדירות רותחות" (boiling pots) settle the matter. רבי יהודה is talking about the very pots the רישא forbade, so he is responding to the רישא and being lenient. Only vinegar and brine are excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: "Come and hear." This introduces a source that answers a question.
"As it was taught" in a ברייתא.

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא proves that רבי יהודה is responding to the רישא and being lenient. In his view, even a boiling pot off the fire does not cook spices, unless sharp liquids such as vinegar or brine are present.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it was taught [in a baraita]:
into all stew pots one may place [spices],
into all pots, even boiling, one may place [spices],
phrases.notes: "Boiling" is the key word that proves the lenient reading.

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ מִדָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ חוֹמֶץ וָצִיר.
phrases.english: except for something that contains vinegar or brine.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה is responding to the רישא and is lenient: even boiling pots are permitted, except those with vinegar or brine.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי יהודה explicitly about boiling pots.

steps.title: רב יוסף thinks salt is like spices
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף assumed that salt follows the rule for spices: it cooks in a כלי ראשון but not in a כלי שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף thought to say: Salt is like a spice, in that in a primary vessel it gets cooked, and in a secondary vessel it does not get cooked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic, salt. רב יוסף proposes that salt follows the same rule as spices.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רב יוסף's view, salt may not be put into a כלי ראשון on שבת, because it cooks there. It may be put into a כלי שני. The phrase "סבר למימר" (thought to say) signals that this view is about to be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: "He thought to say." This signals an initial assumption that will likely be rejected.
A primary vessel: the pot that was on the fire.

phrases.english: so that in a primary vessel, it gets cooked,
and in a secondary vessel, it does not get cooked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the משנה's discussion of spices to salt.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Salt cooks in a כלי ראשון but not in a כלי שני, just like spices.

steps.title: אביי cites רבי חייא: salt cooks even in a secondary vessel
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף using רבי חייא's teaching that salt is unlike spices, because it cooks even in a כלי שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: רבי חייא taught that salt is not like a spice, since it gets cooked even in a secondary vessel!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף by quoting a source from רבי חייא that says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא explicitly says salt is NOT like spices. אביי explains this to mean that salt cooks more easily, even in a כלי שני. If so, putting salt into a כלי שני on שבת would be forbidden, which contradicts רב יוסף's assumption.

keyTerms.meaning: He said to him. This introduces a reply or challenge.
He taught, referring to a ברייתא taught by a תנא.

phrases.english: salt is not like a spice,
for in a secondary vessel it also gets cooked!
phrases.notes: This is אביי's explanation of what "not like a spice" means.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: תָּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's assumption from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that salt is like spices and does not cook in a כלי שני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא from רבי חייא says explicitly that salt is unlike spices, meaning it cooks even in a כלי שני.

steps.title: This disagrees with רב נחמן, who says salt needs long cooking
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the view that salt cooks easily disagrees with רב נחמן, who holds that salt needs as much cooking as ox meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this disagrees with רב נחמן, for רב נחמן said: Salt requires cooking like the meat of an ox.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds an observation: the view just quoted (salt cooks even in a כלי שני) is opposed by רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן holds that salt is very hard to cook, needing as long as tough ox meat. By his view, salt would certainly not cook in a כלי שני. So רבי חייא's teaching, as אביי explained it, and רב נחמן's view are two opposite positions.

keyTerms.meaning: "And it disagrees." This marks that two opinions conflict.
The meat of an ox, which takes a very long time to cook.

steps.whatToRemember: There are two opposite views on salt. רבי חייא, as אביי explains him, holds that salt cooks easily, even in a כלי שני. רב נחמן holds that salt is very hard to cook, like ox meat.
steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute affects whether one may add salt to hot food in a כלי שני on שבת.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rav Nachman,
like the meat of an ox.
phrases.notes: Salt needs a lot of cooking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Notes that the position established in step 6 is disputed by רב נחמן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן holds that salt requires as much cooking as ox meat, opposing רבי חייא's view as explained by אביי.

steps.title: Second version: רב יוסף compares salt to spices
steps.stepSummary: In a second version (איכא דאמרי), רב יוסף assumed salt works like spices: it cooks in a כלי ראשון but not in a כלי שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the story went differently: רב יוסף thought salt is like spices. In a כלי ראשון it cooks, but in a כלי שני it does not cook.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives a second version of the salt discussion from Steps 5–7. It starts again with רב יוסף's assumption, which sets up אביי's reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening is almost the same as the first version: רב יוסף compares salt to spices. What changes in this version is how אביי responds.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say (a second version of the discussion)
He thought to say (an assumption that is about to be challenged)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is the same discussion told a second way. Keep the two versions separate in your head.

phrases.notes: Introduces a second version of the discussion.

phrases.english: that in a primary vessel it gets cooked,
in a secondary vessel it does not get cooked.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: סָבַר רַב יוֹסֵף לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restarts the salt discussion as a second version of Steps 5–7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Salt cooks in a כלי ראשון but not in a כלי שני, just like spices (רב יוסף's assumption).

steps.title: אביי: salt is harder to cook than spices
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes רבי חייא: salt is not like spices, because it does not cook even in a כלי ראשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: רבי חייא taught that salt is not like spices. Salt does not cook even in a כלי ראשון.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף with a teaching of רבי חייא. In this version, salt is harder to cook than spices, not easier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, salt was 'not like spices' because it cooks more easily, even in a כלי שני. Here the same words mean the opposite: salt is tougher and does not cook even in a כלי ראשון. Either way, רב יוסף's comparison of salt to spices is rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught (a תנאי teaching, a ברייתא)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the versions. In version 1, salt cooks easily, even in a כלי שני. In version 2, salt cooks with difficulty, not even in a כלי ראשון.

phrases.english: for even in a primary vessel it does not get cooked,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: תָּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's assumption in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that salt cooks just like spices.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא of רבי חייא says outright that salt is not like spices, because it does not cook even in a כלי ראשון.

steps.title: This version fits רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: In this version, אביי's view matches רב נחמן, who said salt needs as much cooking as ox meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what רב נחמן meant when he said: salt needs to be cooked as long as ox meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the second version fits nicely with רב נחמן's saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, the view that salt cooks easily disagreed with רב נחמן (Step 7). In this version, salt is hard to cook, so it matches רב נחמן exactly. So the second version removes the disagreement.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is the same as (shows agreement with a known statement)

steps.whatToRemember: Version 1: salt cooks easily, which argues with רב נחמן. Version 2: salt is hard to cook, which agrees with רב נחמן.

phrases.english: And that is what Rav Naḥman said:
like the meat of an ox.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's version by linking it to רב נחמן.
steps.raayaObject: That salt is hard to cook (the second version of אביי's view).
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן's saying that salt needs as much cooking as ox meat.

steps.title: משנה: a vessel under a lamp to catch oil
steps.stepSummary: On שבת you may not place a vessel under a lamp to catch dripping oil. If it was placed before שבת it may stay there, but the oil may not be used because it is not prepared for use.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not put a vessel under a lamp on שבת to catch the oil. If it was put there while it was still day (before שבת), it is allowed. Still, one may not use the oil, because it was not set aside for use.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic: putting a vessel in place to catch something on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Placing the vessel on שבת is forbidden. The oil that drips into it is מוקצה, so the vessel would become stuck holding something that may not be moved. Before שבת, placing it is fine. But the oil that drips is still not usable, because it was set aside for burning and not for use on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: While it is still day (before שבת)
Prepared (set aside for use on שבת). The opposite of מוקצה

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה sets up the whole discussion that follows: when may you place a vessel to catch or protect something on שבת?

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין נוֹתְנִין כְּלִי תַּחַת הַנֵּר
phrases.english: MISHNA: One may not place a vessel beneath the lamp
to receive the oil in it.
And if they placed it while it was still day, it is permitted,
but one may not benefit from it
because it is not from what is prepared.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין נוֹתְנִין כְּלִי תַּחַת הַנֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה; a new topic begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No placing a vessel under a lamp on שבת. If it was placed before שבת it may stay, but the dripped oil is מוקצה.

steps.title: רב חסדא: catching an egg is forbidden, covering it is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא: you may not put a vessel under a hen to catch its egg, but you may turn a vessel upside down over the egg so it does not break.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Even though the Sages said you may not put a vessel under a hen to catch its egg, you may turn a vessel over on top of the egg so it won't break.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב חסדא's ruling about an egg, a case similar to the משנה's lamp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the oil, a newly laid egg is מוקצה, so catching it in a vessel is not allowed. Yet covering the egg to protect it is allowed. רב חסדא does not give a reason for the difference. רבה supplies one in Steps 13–14.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: one may not place a vessel beneath a hen
one may overturn a vessel on it
so that it will not break.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the משנה's idea to a similar case: an egg.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No vessel under a hen to catch the egg; you may cover the egg with an upside-down vessel.

steps.title: רבה asks for רב חסדא's reason
steps.stepSummary: רבה asks: what is the reason behind רב חסדא's distinction?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: What is רב חסדא's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה asks why covering the egg is allowed but catching it is not. This sets up his own answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both actions protect the egg, so why treat them differently? רבה wants the principle behind the ruling.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב חסדא allows covering the egg but forbids catching it.

steps.title: Common protection is allowed, rare protection is not
steps.stepSummary: Hens usually lay eggs in garbage heaps, where the eggs get stepped on, and not on slopes. The Sages allowed protection in common situations but not in rare ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that a hen usually lays its egg in a garbage heap, not on a slope. The Sages allowed common protection, but did not allow rare protection.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers his own question. The rule depends on how common the situation is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An egg in a garbage heap getting crushed is common, so covering it is allowed. An egg on a slope rolling away is rare, so placing a vessel under the hen is not allowed. The Sages only bent the rules for protection that people need often.

phrases.english: a hen tends to lay its egg in a garbage heap,
and it does not tend to lay its egg
and uncommon protection they did not permit.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר, תַּרְנְגוֹלֶת עֲשׂוּיָה לְהַטִּיל בֵּיצָתָהּ בָּאַשְׁפָּה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is common versus rare protection. Only common protection was permitted.

steps.title: אביי: a broken barrel of טבל is rare, yet allowed
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה with a ברייתא: if a barrel of טבל breaks on a roof, you may put a vessel under it. That seems to be rare protection, yet it is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: Is it true that rare protection is not allowed? But a ברייתא teaches: if someone's barrel of טבל broke on top of his roof, he may bring a vessel and put it underneath!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's principle with a case that looks like rare protection but is still allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A barrel breaking is not an everyday event, so by רבה's rule protecting it should be forbidden. Also, טבל cannot be eaten on שבת, yet the ברייתא still lets you save it. This seems to show that even rare protection is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him (from a תנאי source)
But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא?
Produce not yet tithed; forbidden to eat

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
And uncommon protection they did not permit?!
If his barrel of untithed produce broke
he brings a vessel and places it beneath it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְהַצָּלָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ מְצוּיָה לֹא הִתִּירוּ
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's rule that rare protection is not permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A barrel breaking seems rare, yet the ברייתא allows placing a vessel under it.

steps.title: New barrels crack often
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the ברייתא is talking about new barrels, which commonly burst. So it is common protection after all.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about new barrels, which often crack.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה's rule is defended. The barrel case is really a common situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: New clay barrels often crack, so catching their contents is common protection. That is why the ברייתא allows it. רבה's principle stays in place.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה's rule: on שבת the Sages allowed placing a vessel to protect something only in common situations, like new barrels that often crack.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא is about new barrels.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A broken barrel is rare, so the ברייתא would show that rare protection is allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: New barrels often crack, so this is common protection. רבה's rule stands.

steps.title: A second challenge: a vessel placed under a lamp to catch sparks
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה again, this time with the משנה that allows placing a vessel under a lamp to catch sparks.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (אביי) challenged him (רבה): Don't we learn that one may place a vessel under a lamp to catch sparks?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a second source to attack רבה's rule. The source allows placing a vessel under a lamp to catch falling sparks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said the Sages allowed protection only for common situations. אביי assumes sparks falling from a lamp are rare. If so, this משנה allows protection in a rare case, which contradicts רבה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him (raised an objection from a source)
Sparks (burning drops of oil falling from the wick)

steps.confusionAlert: The vessel is not being used to put out the fire. It only catches the sparks so they don't cause damage. That is why it counts as 'protection.'

phrases.english: He (אביי) raised an objection to him (רבה):
phrases.notes: Same challenger as Step 15; this is a second attack.

phrases.english: One may place a vessel beneath the lamp
phrases.notes: Quoted from the last משנה of this chapter.
The assumption is that sparks are uncommon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the barrel challenge was answered in Step 16, אביי brings a new source to attack the same rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's rule (Step 14) that the Sages allowed protection only in common situations.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sparks falling from a lamp seem rare, yet the משנה allows placing a vessel to catch them. This would be rare protection being allowed.

steps.title: Answer: sparks are also common
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that sparks falling from a lamp happen often, so this is protection in a common situation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי's challenge by saying sparks happen often. So the משנה fits רבה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer works just like the one in Step 16 about new barrels. It doesn't change רבה's rule. It only shows that אביי's case really belongs in the 'common' category. Sparks from a burning wick are a regular event, so the Sages allowed protecting against them.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה's rule survives two challenges. The Sages allowed protection (like a vessel under a barrel or a lamp) only when the danger is common. Bursting new barrels and falling sparks both count as common. A hen laying an egg on a slope is rare, so you may not place a vessel under it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the rule works: each case is judged by asking whether the danger is common. The same idea answered both of אביי's challenges.

phrases.notes: 'Also' means just like the new barrels in Step 16.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers אביי's challenge in Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifies the case: the situation אביי assumed was rare is actually common.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sparks falling from a lamp are rare, so the משנה allows rare protection.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sparks are common, so the משנה allows only common protection, which fits רבה's rule.
